report.answer_text:
Inflation by the consumer price index (CPI) stayed moderate and fairly stable in 2025, ending the year a little lower than where it started.
Year-end reading: The CPI rose at an annual rate of 2.7% in December 2025, in line with forecasts and unchanged from November.[1] That included a 0.3% rise from the previous month.[2]
Range over the year: Inflation stayed at or below 3% throughout 2025, well below the pandemic peak of 9.1% in June 2022.[1] From memory, it fell to about 2.3% in spring, then rose to about 3% by September. Those monthly figures didn't come from my search.
Tariffs: The CPI climbed for several months in 2025 after the Trump administration's tariff announcements, though the levies didn't reignite inflation as much as some economists had predicted.[1]
Annual average: One source calculates that inflation ran at 2.63% in 2025, measured as the change in the annual average CPI from 2024 to 2025.[3]
Core inflation: Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, rose 0.24% in December, and the year-over-year rate edged up to 2.64%.[4]
Categories: In the BLS data for December, food was up 3.1% year over year, electricity 6.7% and natural gas 10.8%, while gasoline was down 3.4%.[5]
Data gap: Because of the 2025 lapse in appropriations, the BLS couldn't publish October 2025 indexes for most CPI series.[5] That makes some comparisons harder. It also meant that October rent was assumed to show no inflation, which understated shelter inflation across October and November.[4]
Despite the cooler headline numbers, cooling inflation did not translate into price relief[1] for many households, because price levels stayed higher.
